messages:
Amelia: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting 502/504s and connection timeouts to the hosted API since the 03:00 UTC rollout. Sending sample ticket: customer A — 60% of requests failed in the last 10m.

Ravi: I'm on it. Any quick pattern? specific endpoint, model, region?

Amelia: Most errors are on /v1/generate and /v1/chat/completions. Region us-east-1 is hit the most. Logs show a spike starting right after the canary rollout at 03:02.

Jon: Noted. Which canary? The rollout that toggled "prefer_kv_shard" and added model_variant v3-quant?

Amelia: Yeah — Charlie kicked that canary at 03:00.

Charlie: Yup, pilot-canary-37. Canary was 10% for 20m, then ramped to 30% per autoschedule. I paused at 03:10 after initial alerts but looks like damage already.

Elena: Quick dump from the gateway: 
```
gateway: upstream read timeout (read timeout=10s)\nhandler: 502 bad gateway from runtime pool\nmodel-router: failed to select container: incompatible-kv-config
```

Ravi: "incompatible-kv-config" — that rings alarm bells. The new canary changed KV caching/segment layout. If the runtime expects different KV shapes, it could 5xx when loading cached contexts.

Jon: I pulled a runtime log from a failing container: 
```
panic: invalid shard header length
stack: runtime.go:482
error: failed to initialize kv cache for model v3-quant
```

Jon: So the model instance is failing to initialize KV cache on spin-up. That bubbles up into gateway 502s when requests are routed to the new variant.

Ravi: Immediate mitigation: 1) Stop routing traffic to pilot-canary-37 2) Scale down canary replicas to 0 3) Re-enable routing to stable variant. Who can flip the routing flag?

Charlie: I'm rolling back the canary flag now. Running: 
```
# redwoodctl rollout abort --deployment=hosted-api --canary=pilot-canary-37
redwoodctl routing set --route=hosted-api --model=stable --weight=100%
```

ops-bot: deploy rollback initiated by Charlie — pilot-canary-37 -> abort at 03:18 UTC.

Amelia: Support update: tell customers we detected a regression and are rolling back, ETA ~5-10m for full routing recovery.

Elena: While rollback proceeds, recommend adding short-term rate-limiting per-key to prevent thundering herd on restored stable nodes: 
```
api-gateway.conf: rate_limit: 120rpm per api_key
```

Ravi: Agreed. Also set fallback model for gateway so failed container spins don't cause immediate 502 — fallback to stable until healthchecks pass.

Jon: Patch that now: 
```
config patch --service=gateway --set='fallback_model=stable' --reload
```

ops-bot: routing change applied, stable model weight at 100% (03:22 UTC). Health checker: passing for 7/8 pods, one pod restarting.

Amelia: Customers reporting errors dropped by 90% after 03:24. A few individual requests still 502 due to restarting pod.

Charlie: Root cause hypothesis: the canary introduced an incompatible KV serialization change (kv-shard layout) without a migration path. New containers expect a header that older volumes don't have -> init fails -> container unhealthy -> gateway sees 502s.

Jon: Confirmed in logs: the canary runtime image (v3-quant) contains a KV version bump. We missed the upgrade check in the canary job. Need a preflight that validates KV schema compatibility.

Ravi: Action items (short):
- Charlie: Halt further canaries and block that image from autoschedule (DONE).
- Jon: Build a quick compatibility check script to run in the canary preflight (ETA 3h).
- Elena: Add a policy to routing service to enforce health-based weight change (no >10% increase unless >=95% container health) (ETA 6h).
- Amelia: Apologize to impacted customers, offer pro-rated credits and a status page update (in progress).

Amelia: Support note prepared and sent to tier1: "We've rolled back a canary that caused transient 5xx errors in us-east-1. Root cause under investigation. We'll follow up with a postmortem."

support-bot: Created ticket RFR-5234 linking all impacted customer IDs and request logs.

Charlie: Postmortem owners? Jon + Elena to lead technical writeup, Amelia to co-own customer comms. I'll prepare timeline from release system.

Jon: Quick repro steps for SREs: 
1) curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"model":"v3-quant","input":"test"}'
2) Observe pod restart and `panic: invalid shard header length` in runtime logs
3) Check container env var `KV_SCHEMA_VERSION` on canary image (expected: 2, canary has 3)

Elena: Preventative: gate model image promotion on KV_SCHEMA_VERSION compat check against persisted volumes and a canary bootstrap run that simulates cold-start. Add to 1-click promote pipeline.

Ravi: After-action: keep incident open until all health checks stable for 1 hour and tickets updated. Also verify billing/usage for impacted customers to avoid charging for failed requests — finance/chargeback flag.

Amelia: I'll coordinate refunds and support follow-ups. Thanks everyone for fast rollback and triage. :thumbsup:

Charlie: Filing follow-up RFC for canary policy and KV migration steps. Moving to postmortem channel once we draft.

ops-bot: Incident closed for now (routing restored). Reopen if 5xx rates go above baseline.
